researchQuestionGate: Close VRT's fresh-2026 financial, debt/cash and backlog-conversion gaps and determine what customer-concentration evidence remains genuinely unavailable.
summary: Fresh June 2026 SEC evidence closes most of VRT's financial under-acquisition. Q2 2026 net sales were $3.274B (+24.1% YoY); first-half sales were $5.924B (+26.7%) with gross margin 37.7% and net income $887.9M. Cash was $2.811B plus $300M short-term investments, and operating cash flow was $1.867B for six months. Vertiv refinanced/repaid its term loan in March 2026 and held $2.484B of revolver availability; debt now consists principally of $850M secured notes plus $2.1B of long-dated senior notes. Working-capital cash generation was heavily helped by $1.823B of deferred-revenue inflow while inventory rose by about $1.048B, so backlog/order strength is real but conversion quality should not be judged from headline book-to-bill alone. The filing does not provide a comparable named/top-customer concentration table, so that gap remains unknown rather than inferable.

evidence.claim: Q2 2026 net sales were $3.2743B, up 24.1% YoY; first-half 2026 net sales were $5.9238B, up 26.7%, gross profit $2.2346B and net income $887.9M.
At June 30, 2026 cash and cash equivalents were $2.8106B and short-term investments $300M; total current assets were $9.9849B. Revolver availability was $2.4836B net of letters of credit.

Vertiv repaid its term loan in full in March 2026 and replaced prior revolver arrangements. At June 30 debt included $850M Senior Secured Notes due 2028 and four senior-note tranches totaling $2.1B due 2036-2066; the prior ~$2.076B term loan balance was gone.

First-half operating cash flow was $1.8666B versus $626.2M a year earlier. Working capital contributed $678.8M, including a $1.8227B increase in deferred revenue, while inventory consumed $1.048B; capital expenditures were $285.9M.

The filing explicitly warns of unpredictable placing/cancelling of customer orders and failure to realize sales expected from backlog; it does not provide a directly comparable top-customer concentration schedule in this 10-Q.

inference: Liquidity/refinancing risk is materially lower than the stale underwriting note implied: cash plus short-term investments slightly exceed the disclosed par value of the major long-term notes, and revolver capacity is substantial. This does not eliminate leverage risk but changes its character from near-term refinancing dependence to capital-allocation/duration risk.

The large deferred-revenue contribution and inventory build are consistent with strong order intake and advance funding, but they also mean headline operating cash flow contains a material working-capital timing benefit. Chief should separate underlying earnings/cash conversion from customer prepayments when scoring margin/cash-flow quality.

Backlog demand is credible but cancellation/aging quality remains only partially observable. Red-team's warning about book-to-bill and conversion remains valid even after the fresh financials are added.
contradictions: The same-cycle underwriting report described fresh 2026 financials and debt/cash as missing; the June 30 10-Q directly resolves those items.

Very strong cash generation coexists with a $1.048B inventory use and $1.823B deferred-revenue inflow, so a simple OCF headline would overstate normalized cash-conversion quality if working-capital timing is ignored.
unknowns: Comparable current top-customer/end-customer concentration remains undisclosed in the located 10-Q; do not fabricate a percentage from geography or end-market commentary.
Backlog aging, cancellation rights and the portion supported by substantive customer penalties remain insufficiently quantified in this filing.
How much of the current deferred-revenue surge is tied to a small number of hyperscale/colocation projects remains unknown.
A contract-level backlog-quality review of material customer agreements would require additional filings/exhibits or company disclosures.
falsifiers: Deferred-revenue growth reverses while inventory remains elevated and backlog conversion slows.
Material customer cancellations or interconnection/power delays push recognized revenue beyond planned project windows.
Margin improvement fails to persist as capacity expansion and acquisitions raise fixed-cost intensity.
recommendedActionDetail: Promote the fresh financial/liquidity/debt/working-capital facts into VRT underwriting after verification. Keep customer concentration and backlog cancellation/aging as narrow explicit remaining gates rather than treating the whole dossier as financially stale.
